To better assess your risk, have you ever experienced excessive bleeding during surgeries or noticed unusually large bruises without any injury?

speaker: Doctor
text: The bleeding has persisted for over a week, and I've noticed frequent nosebleeds and large bruises on my arms. Have you ever had a family member diagnosed with a bleeding disorder, and did you experience any bleeding issues during your childhood immunizations or minor cuts? REQUEST TEST: Bleeding time, Factor VIII activity, Factor IX activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The bleeding time of 6 minutes is within the normal range, which makes a primary platelet function disorder less likely. Given the prolonged post-extraction bleeding and easy bruising, do you have any history of joint pain, swelling, or deep muscle aches that might suggest a factor deficiency?

REQUEST TEST: Factor X activity, Factor V activity, von Willebrand Factor antigen, and vWF activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal Factor VIII, IX, X, V, von Willebrand antigen, and activity results, combined with a normal bleeding time, effectively rule out the common hereditary bleeding disorders like hemophilia and von Willebrand disease.

Given the persistent bleeding and easy bruising with all these specific tests coming back normal, have you ever noticed bleeding into the skin or joints after minor trauma, and do you have a history of anemia or fatigue?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC), Fibrinogen, and Thrombin_Time.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC shows normal platelet count and hemoglobin, and your PT, aPTT, bleeding time, and fibrinogen are all within normal limits, which effectively rules out common platelet disorders, coagulation factor deficiencies, and consumptive coagulopathies like DIC. Given the persistent bleeding and easy bruising despite normal standard coagulation workup, have you taken any medications such as aspirin, NSAIDs, or anticoagulants, and do you have any personal or family history of liver disease?

REQUEST TEST: Liver function tests (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase) and Liver Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The liver function tests and ultrasound results are normal, so liver disease is not the cause of your bleeding. Given your normal coagulation profile, normal platelet function, and lack of liver pathology, have you been taking any over-the-counter pain relievers like aspirin or ibuprofen regularly?

REQUEST TEST: Medication review; please list all current medications, supplements, and herbal remedies.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your liver function is normal and standard coagulation tests are within limits, I need to rule out a platelet function disorder or a localized vessel issue. Have you been taking any over-the-counter pain relievers like aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen? Additionally, do you experience bleeding that is not visible, such as blood in your urine or stool?

REQUEST TEST: Platelet Function Analyzer (PFA-100).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The PFA-100 results are normal, which is very unusual given your persistent bleeding and easy bruising despite a completely normal standard coagulation panel. I have exhausted the standard laboratory workup; have you noticed any recent infections, viral symptoms like fever or fatigue, or any new medications you might be taking that aren't standard pain relievers?

REQUEST TEST: Viral Serology (Parvovirus B19, Hepatitis B & C, HIV) and detailed medication/supplement history review.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The viral serology is negative, and since your comprehensive coagulation profile, platelet function, and liver function are all normal, we must consider acquired or localized vascular causes. Have you recently started any new herbal supplements, have you noticed any thinning of your blood vessels (telangiectasia) or small red spots on your skin (petechiae), and do you have a family history of telangiectasias or recurrent nosebleeds?

REQUEST TEST: ANCA, Anti-GBM antibodies; REQUEST IMAGES: Skin examination (look for petechiae or telangiectasias).
